sources.title: Geological map of Greenland 1:2 500 000
sources.authors: Jan C. Escher and T. Christopher R. Pulvertaft
sources.publisher: Geological Survey of Greenland (GGU); official digital copy hosted by GEUS
sources.page: Single map sheet, PDF page 1; southwestern Inland Ice, Isukasia–Ivisartoq–Nuuk marginal region, readable graticule and Inland Ice legend.
sources.supports: Regional ice-sheet and marginal feature-class context, distinguishing glacier, fjord and settlement names from evidence of a named river.
sources.limits: Regional geological mapping, not a river gazetteer or hydrological survey. It supports the feature-class scope conclusion, not proof of natural flow, connectivity or formal river identity. The historical ice margin is not asserted to be its current position.
sources.reuse_limit: GEUS custom terms allow internal research but restrict redistribution and new maps based on the data. The original map and local crops remain private; only own factual notes and public bibliography are intended for publication.

sources.title: Relatório de Monitoramento da Qualidade das Águas, RPGA Rio Mucuri, 1ª Campanha – 2013
sources.publisher: Governo do Estado da Bahia, Instituto do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (INEMA)

correspondence: All three selected mainstem pieces were inspected. The eastern interior beginning runs northwest, the middle makes an undulating westward traverse and then a northwestward rise, and the western portion bends southwest into the marginal region. There is no separately selected tributary piece.

The long eastern and middle portions correspond to the mapped Inland Ice. The western turn approaches the adjoining marginal terrain in the Isukasia–Ivisartoq and inner Nuup Kangerlua region northeast of Nuuk. The map graticule and regional ice/land arrangement support that feature-class context, not an exact terminal stream, lake, glacier or fjord boundary.

The readable map does not establish the whole modeled path as a named natural river. A nearby fjord, glacial or marginal-watercourse name cannot be extended across the interior-ice traverse. This scope hold does not assert that every local marginal stream is unnamed.

The source legend distinguishes ice-surface contours, dashed thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and bold blue aeromagnetic lineaments south of 68°N. These are not named river channels. Historical mapping does not establish current ice margins or actual surface/subglacial connectivity along the model line.

correspondence.finding: The selection starts with a short eastern approach, northward detour and westward lake-loop course before descending south. Anderson's Figure 96 shows the relevant northern lake complex and distinguishes Gates and Ross lakes, but it does not resolve that exact initial modeled connection reliably. Neither lake is assigned as a proven selected passage, and no conventional river-source description replaces the selected beginning.

The subsequent southward course corresponds regionally to the mapped upper lake chain containing Morris and Surf lakes, then bends southeast and east north of the Smallwood setting. Its long southern arc and final northeast turn agree with the trunk shown in the Fisheries maps; the retained Quebec sheet supplies additional unlabeled watercourse context. Exact lake entry and exit positions are not assigned.

The selected western piece reaches the Shipiskan–Kanairiktok junction from the southwest. Figure 96 places Shipiskan Lake on the separate northern approach, and the provincial district description explicitly locates the junction southeast of that lake. The selection therefore must not be described as traversing Shipiskan Lake merely because the CANAL profile describes that lake within the wider Kanairiktok system.

East of the junction, the selected large river loop, eastward Snegamook Lake passage and northeast lower-river course match the readable Fisheries maps. Snegamook is explicitly identified in both map and river description. Pocketknife Lake and the separate northern tributaries are contextual branches, not selected mainstem passages.

The lower selection follows the distinct bend below the Snegamook corridor and continues to the inner Kanairiktok Bay estuary setting. The Fisheries maps distinguish the lower river, mouth falls and bay; Murphy also provides a labeled estuary photograph. No exact modern river–estuary boundary, tidal limit or full bay traversal is established.
The southeastern beginning follows the mapped Río Chilamayo east of Imata into the upper Colca corridor. The neighboring Chili/Sumbay route is distinct.
The selection passes the Los Españoles setting, continues northwest through the Condoroma reservoir corridor, then bends toward Tisco and south to Sibayo and Tuti.
The westward canyon route agrees through the Yanque–Cabanaconde sector, past the Molloco junction and Choco, toward the Ayo/Mamacocha junction setting. Those tributary branches are not selected.
The southwestern turn continues into the southward Río Majes valley and the Corire corridor.
The lower selection follows Río Camaná to the Pacific coastal setting near Camaná and San José, west of the separate Quilca outlet.

The western start follows the channel labelled Córrego Mumbuca on the Ladainha municipal map and joins Rio Mucuri do Norte. The separately mapped northern continuation of Mucuri do Norte is not the selected initial branch.

The selection continues east through the Ladainha municipal area, south of the municipal seat, along Mucuri do Norte. The state map shows its connection with the separately named Mucuri do Sul and the ensuing Rio Mucuri course turning northeast past the Mucuri district. The southern Malacacheta source route is not selected.
The subsequent east-to-southeast corridor agrees with Rio Mucuri through the Carlos Chagas and Nanuque settings. Rio Todos os Santos is a distinct incoming tributary, not the selected upstream route.

The Bahia continuation follows the Mucuri below the Santa Clara–Nanuque setting, crosses the BR-101 monitoring location, and reaches the lower estuarine corridor beside Mucuri town on the Atlantic coast. The map supports coastal identity without assigning an exact mouth or tidal boundary.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
